peripheral_horizon.interpretation: PIO is the dominant exclusive one-cycle limiter; UART is secondary and DMA is almost entirely negligible or overlapped

cpu_decode.interpretation: decode reuse is nearly universal, but dynamic straight-line runs are short; a block cache remains plausible but has a smaller grouping span and belongs to OPT3

ranking.lever: PIO exact event horizon and bulk advance
ranking.reason: PIO alone occupies 217025266 cycles, 70.25 percent of running cycles, and must be solved before the largest running batches can exist
UART-only plus UART-DMA overlap occupies 40197601 cycles; useful after PIO no longer fixes the horizon at one cycle
99.83 percent cache hits show reuse, but the mean sequential hit run is only 4.56 instructions and only 13.52 percent of hit mass lies in runs of at least 16
DMA-only occupancy is only 22000 cycles and most DMA occupancy overlaps UART

decision.selected_next_prototype: PIO exact event horizon and bulk advance
decision.next_gate: prove exact PIO state, pin transition, device response, DREQ and IRQ equivalence before any wall-time measurement
